<translate>
<!--T:1-->
Every record in openCR has '''main data''' with its basic information, and '''sections''' for information that can occur more than once. An artwork, for example, can have several titles, several measurements (image, sheet, frame) and a long ownership history; each of these is a list of entries in its own section.

<!--T:2-->
This page lists the sections of each entity, named as they appear on the record's page. In ''Edit Mode'', a pencil at the top of the page opens the main data in a pop-up; the plus icon next to a section's heading adds an entry, the pencil before an entry changes it, and the bin after it deletes it. Most pages also have the blocks ''Sources'' and ''Notes'' (see [[Sources and citations]]). For the overall picture, see [[How openCR is structured]].

<!--T:3-->
== Objects (artworks) ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What goes there
|-
| Materials & Techniques || What the work is made of: oil, canvas, paper, acrylic, etching and so on
|-
| Attributes || Marks and inscriptions: signed, dated, numbered, stamped, with their location and the text on the work
|-
| Dimensions || The dimensions, one row per measured part (for example image, sheet, frame)
|-
| Parts of the object || The named parts of a multi-part work, such as the panels of a triptych
|-
| Editions || The editions of a print: regular edition, artist's proofs, trial proofs and so on
|-
| Copies || The casts or copies of a sculpture or multiple
|-
| Individual copies || Single physical copies, such as one cast or one impression, each entered on a page of its own
|-
| Other Titles || Further titles of the work: alternative, translated, or as used in a particular publication
|-
| Agents || People and institutions involved with the work: printer, publisher, foundry, photographer, co-author
|-
| Dates || Dated events in the life of the work, such as signing, printing or restoration
|-
| Exhibitions || The exhibitions where the work was shown
|-
| Provenance || The ownership history
|-
| Transactions || Sales and auctions
|-
| References || The literature that mentions or reproduces the work
|-
| Tags || The artist's tags and the general tags that apply to this work
|-
| Related objects || Links to other works: study for, copy of, version of and similar
|-
| Notes || Remarks on the work, public or private
|}
The images are shown in the left-hand column of the page. In ''Edit Mode'', ''Upload an image'' adds one and ''Images management'' lists them (see [[Objects#Images|Images]]).

<!--T:4-->
== Artists ==
The artist's home page shows the main data. The sections are on the details page, ''More artist details'':
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What goes there
|-
| Contact details || Phone numbers, email addresses, websites, social media
|-
| Alias of the artist || The alternative names: translations, pseudonyms and other spellings of the artist's name
|-
| Artist - Relations with the directory || Links to people and institutions: gallerist, publisher, family, mentor, heir and others
|-
| Publications used as reference || The pages where publications discuss the artist
|-
| Artist - selected languages || The languages the artist's catalogue is meant to be published in (shown in ''Edit Mode'' only)
|-
| Template Management || Templates with materials and techniques for new artworks (shown to the artist's editors only)
|-
| Definition of categories || The object types that this catalogue assigns to another category than the general mapping, used for filtering the catalogue
|-
| Artist specific Tags || The artist's own keywords for grouping artworks
|-
| Artist - additional descriptions || The biographies, one per language and type (life biography or art-historical biography)
|}

<!--T:5-->
== Publications ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What goes there
|-
| Agents || Authors, editors, publishers and other contributors
|-
| Used Languages || The languages the publication is written in
|-
| Related artists || The artists the publication is about; they put it into their bibliography and decide who may edit it
|-
| References to artists || The pages where the publication discusses each artist
|-
| Related events || Events the publication documents, for example the exhibition an exhibition catalogue accompanies
|-
| Related Publications || Links to other publications: part of, version of, copy or facsimile of, based on and similar
|-
| Referenced Objects || The artworks that cite this publication
|-
| Publication Images || Images of the publication, such as its cover
|}

<!--T:6-->
== Events ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What goes there
|-
| Related artists || The artists who took part, and their relation to the event
|-
| Related agents || The people and institutions involved: organiser, curator, gallery, sponsor
|-
| Places and dates || Where and when the event took place; a touring exhibition has several
|-
| Related publications || Publications documenting the event
|-
| Description || A text about the event, one per language
|-
| Related objects || The artworks shown, with the reference, the lender and the title used in the exhibition
|-
| Event Images || Images of the event, such as installation views or posters
|}

<!--T:7-->
== Directory ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! What goes there
|-
| Address || The primary address; in ''Edit Mode'', a link to the page ''Addresses'' with all addresses, each with its type and period of validity
|-
| Contact details || Phone numbers, email addresses, websites
|-
| Activities || What the person or institution does: gallery, publisher, photographer, curator and so on
|-
| Related persons and organizations || Links between directory entries, for example between a person and an institution
|-
| Related events || The events in which the entry took part, with its role
|-
| Description || A text about the entry
|}
The page also lists where the entry appears in other records. These lists are filled from those records (''Collection of objects'' cannot be changed at present): ''Relations with Artist'', ''Publications (as editor)'', ''Publications (as author)'', ''Collection of objects'', ''Objects in property'' (from ownership histories), ''Agent'' and ''Named on works''.
</translate>
